Pete Hegseth, Gage Skidmore , CC BY-SA 4.0 , via Wikimedia Commons Three American foreign policy experts who held senior positions in the U.S. government — during the George W. Bush and Bill Clinton administrations — are criticizing President Trump and the Pentagon for considering a withdrawal of approximately 25,000 U.S. soldiers from Europe, despite warnings from NATO allies about the growing threat of Russian aggression. The former officials argue against the withdrawal in a new Foreign Affairs article titled ‘The Crumbling Defense of Europe: Trump Has Already Undermined NATO and Allied Deterrence.’ [NOTE: The Trump administration argues it’s time for Europe to “stand on its own feet” and defend itself, and that the U.S. should now focus its military resources on the Middle East and Asia.] “There is no logical or military reason for the United States to withdraw from Europe. Instead, the only plausible explanation is a decidedly illogical one: Trump hates the continent,” write Franklin Miller, Eric Edelman, and Walter Slocombe. https://t.co/4awCQ7Y5fJ — Foreign Affairs (@ForeignAffairs) September 17, 2026 The three former Defense Department leaders who wrote the article are: Franklin Miller , who served 31 years in the U.S. government, including the Department of State, the Department of Defense and as a Special Assistant to President George W. Bush; Walter Slocombe , former Under Secretary of Defense for Policy during the Clinton administration; and Eric Edelman , former Under Secretary of Defense for Policy (2005–2009), U.S. Ambassador to Turkey (2003–2005), U.S. Ambassador to Finland (1998–2001), and Principal Deputy Assistant to the Vice President for National Security Affairs (2001–2003). In the Foreign Affairs article, they write: “There is no logical or military reason for the United States to withdraw from Europe. Instead, the only plausible explanation is a decidedly illogical one: Trump hates the continent.” The experts warn that the withdrawal “could even threaten the American homeland. The administration’s planned pullback is not motivated by any meaningful appreciation for alliance management, threat analysis, or historical understanding. Instead, it is the product of sheer bias against Europe, which makes it as damning as it is dangerous.” [NOTE: On Thursday, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, wrote a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio (who also serves as the national security advisor) to ask that relevant U.S. ambassadors (including those in the Baltic nations of Estonia, Lithuania and Latvia) get involved in the Europe troop review, which the Pentagon initiated in June.] "Shaheen wrote that adjustments in troop levels would have an effect on bilateral relationships ​that the State ⁠Department would be left to manage, with the Baltic nations of Estonia, Lithuania and Latvia among the countries with the most at stake."
